jobs.title: Senior Director Enterprise Architecture & Ontology
jobs.description:
A career as a Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture & Ontology within the Enterprise Architecture team at National Bank means acting as the Senior Director responsible for Enterprise Architecture and Integrated Enterprise Knowledge. It means contributing to the definition and evolution of a strategic practice that provides a better understanding of the relationships between business capabilities, processes, data, applications, interfaces, technologies, and controls. This role allows you to make a positive impact on our organization through your expertise in enterprise architecture, semantic modelling, and organizational transformation supported by artificial intelligence and automation.

Your job

Shape
the evolution of the enterprise architecture practice by defining
directions, methods, standards, and priorities that support
decision-making and organizational transformation.

Define
and evolve an enterprise ontology that connects business capabilities,
processes, data, applications, interfaces, technology components, and
controls through clear semantics and governed relationships.

Establish
modelling principles, governance mechanisms, and accountabilities that
enable different teams to contribute to a shared, reliable, and reusable
understanding of the enterprise.

Leverage
artificial intelligence and automation to discover and reconcile
relationships across LeanIX, the CMDB, and other authoritative sources
without creating a new monolithic repository, while ensuring information
quality, governance, and traceability.

Transform
the enterprise ontology into products, views, integrations, and use cases
that support strategic planning, impact analysis, technology decisions,
and transformation initiatives.

Represent
the practice in architecture and delivery forums, engage stakeholders, and
measure adoption, coverage, and value delivered to adjust priorities based
on the organization’s needs.

Your team

The Enterprise Architecture practice brings together
specialists who work collaboratively to develop an integrated understanding of
the organization and support its transformation. You work closely with
architecture, business, data, technology, and platform teams.

Within the Enterprise Architecture sector, you report
to the Bank’s Chief Architect. You contribute to transforming knowledge that is
currently distributed across multiple teams, repositories, and tools into a
coherent, accessible, and actionable view that supports decision-making.

We aim to provide you with maximum flexibility to
enhance your quality of life. This includes a hybrid work environment as well
as a flexible and adaptable schedule.

The Bank values continuous development and internal
mobility. Our personalized training programs, based on learning through
experience, help you master your role and develop new areas of expertise.
Resources such as the Data Academy, language training, the Harvard Learning
Center, as well as coaching and mentoring support, are available to you at all
times.

Prerequisites

University
degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field and at least
ten years of relevant experience in enterprise or solution architecture.

In-depth
expertise in enterprise ontology, semantic modelling, or knowledge graphs,
as well as modelling relationships between business and technology assets.

Strong
command of enterprise architecture repositories and authoritative sources,
including LeanIX and CMDBs.

Expertise
in information governance, data quality, traceability, and the
reconciliation of data from multiple sources.

Hands-on
experience with artificial intelligence and automation applied to
relationship discovery, knowledge quality improvement, and the delivery of
enterprise capabilities.

Strong
understanding of integration architectures, application programming
interfaces (APIs), event-driven architectures, cloud computing, and
digital ecosystems.

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to discuss frequently with our service providers or partners who speak a language other than French.
Required skills: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, Critical Thinking, Cross-functional Collaboration, Enterprise Architecture, Enterprise Integration, Influencing Skills, Information Governance, Innovation Management, Knowledge Graph, Micro Focus UCMDB, Model Making, Ontologies, Semantics, Strategic Vision, Strategy Execution

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

Making a bold move in a people-first environment

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. Requirements

Description & Requirements

Technology Director | Global Sourcing Technology

Who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

Global Supply Chain Technology delivers the platforms and capabilities that power lululemon’s supply chain—from raw material innovation and development, costing, sourcing, quality, sustainability and traceability, trade, logistics, and distribution technology. Our team works in close partnership with core business units to ensure that our supply chain remains agile, efficient, and responsive to ever-evolving market demands. By continuously innovating and refining our technological solutions, we enable best-in-class supply chain operations to service our Guests and our stores. This collaborative approach ensures we provide exceptional experiences and support lululemon’s growth in every community we serve.

The role

We are seeking a Technology Director to define and execute the multi year strategy for modernizing and transforming lululemon’s global sourcing technology ecosystem. This leader will shape the strategic roadmap, elevate costing and sourcing platform capabilities, advance AI driven decisioning, and ensure operational excellence across the systems that connect lululemon to its global vendor base.

You will own all aspects of technology for Global Sourcing—architecture, engineering, security, QA automation, operations, and delivery—and oversee a globally distributed team across North America and India. You will be accountable for the platforms that support approximately 300 raw material (RM) and finished goods (FG) vendors globally, and will partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on the technology evolution required to support enterprise initiatives. This role requires a seasoned leader with a proven record of developing a strong leadership bench, managing complex solutions, and thriving in complex, fast paced, and highly collaborative environments.

This Role Oversees Technology Solutions Supporting

Product costing and should-cost modelling (materials, labor, overhead, landed cost)
Sourcing execution (quoting and RFQ, vendor award, capacity allocation and booking)
Purchase order management and order lifecycle for raw material and finished goods
Supplier collaboration portals and vendor-facing self-service
Partner connectivity (vendors, mills, agents, service providers)
Integration frameworks (EDI, APIs, event-driven architecture)
Master data and data quality for cost
Sourcing analytics, margin visibility, exception management, and operational dashboards

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Roadmap

Define and deliver a multi year global sourcing technology strategy that enhances scalability, reliability, and speed to market.
Translate business needs into an actionable engineering roadmap incorporating modernization, cloud migration, supplier collaboration, and responsible AI adoption.
Partner with business Directors, Sr. Directors, and VPs across Global Sourcing and Costing to define, deliver, and support the strategic roadmap.
Enroll cross functional technology partners in the strategic vision for Global Sourcing, and lead the creation and expansion of new capabilities that align with our strategic goals.

Platform & Architecture Modernization

Modernize existing costing and sourcing platforms and integrate next generation capabilities (costing engines, sourcing execution suites, or equivalent).
Drive transformation toward API-first, event-driven, and scalable integration architectures across the global vendor base.
Lead design and implementation of secure, resilient, and responsible data management and governance frameworks for material, vendor, and cost master data.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on technology evolution that supports enterprise initiatives.

Engineering Leadership

Lead globally distributed engineering, QA automation, delivery, and support teams; develop managers and future-ready technical leaders.
Serve as the escalation point for Technology Managers to support delivery, making thoughtful decisions on the fly and constantly clearing roadblocks.
Raise engineering standards around quality, observability, security, and system reliability.
Build high performing, diverse teams with a culture of inclusion, transparency, and continuous improvement, and support career progression and stretch opportunities across the Global Sourcing technology area.

Operational Excellence

Oversee delivery, operations, and vendor/partner management across sourcing and costing systems, and own the relationship with key vendor partners.
Manage budgets for strategic initiatives and baseline opex for Global Sourcing technology, ensuring clear ROI and optimization of total cost of ownership.
Drive root cause analysis, systems reliability, service maturity, and measurable operational improvements.

Innovation & AI Enablement

Introduce AI-driven decision support for should-cost modelling, quote analysis, capacity allocation, vendor performance, and exception management.
Champion ethical, transparent, and responsible use of AI in sourcing and vendor-facing operations.

Qualifications

Experience leading large scale initiatives and modernization efforts for supply chain platforms, with highly valued experience in costing and sourcing areas.

Strong background in integration architectures (API platforms, EDI, message streaming, event-driven design).

Demonstrated ability to manage large budgets and deliver high-impact technology programs.
Exceptional communication, storytelling, and executive influencing skills.
Continuous learning mindset that stays on the leading edge of sourcing and supply chain technology solutions that can bring value to the organization.
Experience with AI/ML use cases in supply chain, sourcing, or costing.
Understanding of apparel or consumer goods product development, raw materials, and global vendor management processes.
Experience working with distributed teams across multiple time zones and a global vendor base.

Success Metrics

Reduced sourcing and purchase order cycle times, with fewer manual touches per order.
Improved reliability, uptime, and SLA performance of sourcing and costing systems.

jobs.title: Head of Platform & Infrastructure Engineering
jobs.description:
Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future.

We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you!

The Role

In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include:

Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.
Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).
Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!
Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.
Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.
You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.
If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!

The Qualifications

We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.
You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.
You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.
You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team.
You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.
You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe.
You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.

What We’re Building

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better
at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

Why You Shouldn’t Apply

You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.
You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.
You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).
You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.
To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.
You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.

Engineering Culture

Our Engineering Culture Is Motivated By Benji’s (Co-founder And CEO) And My Belief That a Small, Talented Team, Given The Right Environment, Can Build High-quality Software Fast (and Work Regular Hours!). We Do It Through

Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design
Natural collaboration and deliberate communication
Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.
Putting effort into building a diverse team

Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive .

Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).

To Drive It Home, Here's a Recent Calendar Of An Engineer Who Has Been With Us For Over 4 Years. ~34 Hours Of Focus Time, 2.5h Of Interviews, And 3.5 Hours Of Meetings

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

Increase Leverage, not Team Size

We Built Ashby With The Quality, Breadth, And Depth That Many Customers Would Expect From Much Larger Teams Over Larger Time Scales. We’ve Done This Through Investment In

Great developer tooling. For example, our CI/CD takes ~10m, we deploy at least 15x a day, and our debugger works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.
Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).
AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. The Greater Vernon Museum & Archives (GVMA) is seeking an energetic, collaborative, and strategic Executive Director (ED) to lead the organization, strengthen its relationships throughout the community, and help shape the future of the Society as we transition the Museum into the new Greater Vernon Cultural Centre (GVCC).

Who We Are:

Having celebrated our 75th anniversary in 2025, the Greater Vernon Museum and Archives stands as a testament to the vision of its founders, Charles Edward Haines, David Howrie Sr., and W.C. Pound, a pioneering taxidermist who gifted his collection to the City of Vernon. From humble beginnings in a local high school, the museum has grown into a thriving cultural hub, moving through various locations and reaching key milestones along the way, including formalizing our Board of Directors in 1970 and becoming a not-for-profit organization in 2016. Today, we continue to enrich the Greater Vernon area by collecting, preserving, exhibiting, and interpreting its unique artifacts and history. Our collections include over 25,000 physical items and an additional 25,000 objects in our archives, including maps, photos, and video and audio clips.

The Greater Vernon Archives has the distinction of being among the most respected research facilities in the province. Each year, well in excess of 700 research inquiries from individuals in the province and many other parts of the country come through our archives. The Archives acquires and preserves material of archival and/or informational value to the North Okanagan and makes most of this material available to the public by employing accepted archival practices.

Looking forward, we are excited to be moving into the Greater Vernon Cultural Centre, a dynamic cultural hub for the region, co-locating three important venues: the Vernon Public Art Gallery, the Greater Vernon Museum, and an intimate presentation and event space. It will also create a new experience, the cultural commons, a shared social forum where visitors can start their journey or connect with friends and neighbors.

The Opportunity:

Reporting to the Board of Directors through the President, the ED provides strategic and operational leadership to the organization while helping guide its participation in the planning, development, and transition to the Greater Vernon Cultural Centre.

The ED works closely with the GVMA Board, staff, volunteers, the Regional District of North Okanagan (RDNO), municipal and community partners, and other stakeholders to identify needs, establish effective relationships, and support the fulfillment of the Society’s vision and mission.

As we prepare to move into the GVCC in 2027, and open to the public in 2028, a key priority will be leading the transition into the new building and ensuring programs and processes are set up to meet the needs of the community in the new space. This will include clarifying roles and responsibilities, identifying shared services and resources, establishing effective communication and decision-making processes, and developing practical ways for the organizations and other partners to work together seamlessly while maintaining their distinct mandates and identities.

The ED is an important public-facing representative of the GVMA and a collaborative partner in advancing the Cultural Centre’s vision and contribution to the Greater Vernon community.

Key Responsibilities of the Executive Director:

1.     Strategic and Organizational Leadership

Provide operational leadership to GVMA, implementing the strategic plan and developing operational plans for staff.
Oversee museum operations, programming, collections, archives, facilities, and visitor experience.
Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and forward-thinking organizational culture.
Providing recommendations to the board to identify opportunities to strengthen GVMA’s visibility, relevance, and contribution to the community.

2.     GVCC Planning and Transition

Lead the GVMA’s engagement with community partners throughout the planning and transition to the GVCC.
Identify GVMA’s operational, staffing, financial, facility, and service needs within the new shared space.
Collaborate with GVCC partners to develop a sustainable operating model, including roles, responsibilities, governance, shared resources, communication, and decision-making processes.
Support transition planning, operational readiness, and the development of agreements and protocols required for operating multiple sites.

3.     Community Engagement

Represent GVMA positively and professionally to government, community organizations, Indigenous communities, educational institutions, funders, donors, and cultural partners.
Develop and maintain strong, respectful, and mutually beneficial community relationships.
Engage diverse stakeholders to understand needs, gather feedback, identify opportunities, and support informed decision-making.
Participate in relevant committees, working groups, and initiatives related to GVMA and GVCC.

4.     Financial Management, Fundraising and Revenue Development

Develop and oversee annual operating budgets, financial plans, and expenditure controls, while working in collaboration with the Treasurer and Finance Committee.
Oversee grant applications, fundraising, donor development, sponsorships, and revenue-generating initiatives.
Support financial planning for the GVCC transition, including shared costs, funding requirements, and revenue opportunities.
Ensure sound financial stewardship and compliance with applicable requirements.

5.     People, Culture and Organizational Development

Lead, support, and develop staff, contractors, and volunteers.
Oversee recruitment, performance management, training and development, and succession planning.
Maintain human resources policies and the employee handbook to ensure equitable and fair treatment of all employees, while working in collaboration with the HR Committee.
Promote a respectful, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.

6.     Operations, Programming and Visitor Experience

Oversee the effective day-to-day operation of GVMA and the delivery of high-quality services and programs.
Support exhibitions, educational activities, events, research, and community programming.
Ensure the responsible stewardship, preservation, and interpretation of collections and archival resources.
Promote an engaging, welcoming, accessible, and inclusive visitor experience that match the needs of Greater Vernon.

7.     Governance and Accountability

Report regularly to the Board of Directors on operations, financial performance, strategic priorities and risks, while also collaborating frequently with the Board President.
Prepare reports, recommendations, and supporting materials for Board meetings and the Annual General Meeting.
Maintain effective communication with the RDNO and other relevant governing and funding bodies.
Implement Board-approved policies, strategic directions, and initiatives.
Ensure compliance with the Society’s Constitution, Bylaws, policies, and applicable legislation.

Required Qualifications and Experience:

The ideal candidate will be an experienced and collaborative leader who can balance organizational stewardship with the relationship-building, planning, and change leadership required to support GVMA's future. The following are the desired education, skills and experience:

A bachelor’s degree in museum studies, history, business administration, public administration, non-profit management, arts administration, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and relevant leadership experience may be considered.
A minimum of five years of progressive management or leadership experience in a museum, cultural institution, nonprofit organization, public-sector organization, or related environment.
Demonstrated experience providing strategic and operational leadership in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
Experience developing and managing operating budgets, financial plans, funding proposals, and grant applications.
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining effective relationships with community organizations, government representatives, funders, donors, and other stakeholders.
Strong communication, negotiation, facilitation, and relationship-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to engage diverse groups, understand competing needs, build consensus, and move collaborative initiatives forward.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, develop, and retain staff and volunteers.
Experience leading or supporting organizational change, strategic planning, facility development, organizational growth, or a significant transition is an asset.
A commitment to ethical leadership, accountability, inclusion, accessibility, and respect for diverse cultures, abilities, and backgrounds.

.

Identify capability and capacity gaps, oversee recruitment and onboarding activities, and promote knowledge sharing and best practices across the team

Respond to complex and time-sensitive requests from internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a high standard of service and professionalism
Oversee the preparation and dissemination of quarterly and annual reporting, performance dashboards, and stakeholder communications
Ensure high standards of quality, consistency, accuracy, and timeliness across all reporting outputs and program deliverables

Portfolio & Ecosystem Leadership

Build and maintain strong relationships with fund managers, institutional investors, ecosystem stakeholders, and government partners
Represent BDC Capital and Government Funds at industry conferences, panels, events, and stakeholder forums
Stay closely connected to venture capital trends, market developments, and emerging opportunities to support strategic decision-making
Support and lead thought leadership initiatives, market studies, and research projects that generate insights from government investment programs and portfolio activities

What We Are Looking For

Experience and qualifications

Minimum of a Bachelor degree in Commerce or a related discipline (finance, accounting, law or business administration preferred), or an equivalent combination of academic training and relevant professional experience
10 years+ experience in venture capital, private equity, or growth investing, with direct exposure to deal-making at the fund level as well as investment underwriting, structuring, business and legal negotiations and execution
Demonstrated expertise in venture capital fund structures, LPAs, governance frameworks, and policy-driven investment programs
Demonstrated ability to lead complex negotiations and manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously
Significant experience serving on LPACs, Boards of Directors, or equivalent governance bodies
Ability to manage complex stakeholder relationships involving fund managers, institutional investors, government representatives, and senior executives
Strong understanding of the Canadian venture capital ecosystem and a well-established network of industry relationships
Experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams

Core competencies

Strong strategic and investment judgment
Demonstrated leadership and people management capabilities
Excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills
Ability to align operational execution with broader policy, program, and organizational objectives
High level of rigour, organization, and attention to detail
Ability to operate effectively in a complex, fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environment
Collaborative mindset with a commitment to team development, knowledge sharing, and excellence

The Greater Vernon Museum & Archives (GVMA) is seeking an energetic, collaborative, and strategic Executive Director (ED) to lead the organization, strengthen its relationships throughout the community, and help shape the future of the Society as we transition the Museum into the new Greater Vernon Cultural Centre (GVCC).

Who We Are:

Having celebrated our 75th anniversary in 2025, the Greater Vernon Museum and Archives stands as a testament to the vision of its founders, Charles Edward Haines, David Howrie Sr., and W.C. Pound, a pioneering taxidermist who gifted his collection to the City of Vernon. From humble beginnings in a local high school, the museum has grown into a thriving cultural hub, moving through various locations and reaching key milestones along the way, including formalizing our Board of Directors in 1970 and becoming a not-for-profit organization in 2016. Today, we continue to enrich the Greater Vernon area by collecting, preserving, exhibiting, and interpreting its unique artifacts and history. Our collections include over 25,000 physical items and an additional 25,000 objects in our archives, including maps, photos, and video and audio clips.

The Greater Vernon Archives has the distinction of being among the most respected research facilities in the province. Each year, well in excess of 700 research inquiries from individuals in the province and many other parts of the country come through our archives. The Archives acquires and preserves material of archival and/or informational value to the North Okanagan and makes most of this material available to the public by employing accepted archival practices.

Looking forward, we are excited to be moving into the Greater Vernon Cultural Centre, a dynamic cultural hub for the region, co-locating three important venues: the Vernon Public Art Gallery, the Greater Vernon Museum, and an intimate presentation and event space. It will also create a new experience, the cultural commons, a shared social forum where visitors can start their journey or connect with friends and neighbors.

The Opportunity:

Reporting to the Board of Directors through the President, the ED provides strategic and operational leadership to the organization while helping guide its participation in the planning, development, and transition to the Greater Vernon Cultural Centre.

The ED works closely with the GVMA Board, staff, volunteers, the Regional District of North Okanagan (RDNO), municipal and community partners, and other stakeholders to identify needs, establish effective relationships, and support the fulfillment of the Society’s vision and mission.

As we prepare to move into the GVCC in 2027, and open to the public in 2028, a key priority will be leading the transition into the new building and ensuring programs and processes are set up to meet the needs of the community in the new space. This will include clarifying roles and responsibilities, identifying shared services and resources, establishing effective communication and decision-making processes, and developing practical ways for the organizations and other partners to work together seamlessly while maintaining their distinct mandates and identities.

The ED is an important public-facing representative of the GVMA and a collaborative partner in advancing the Cultural Centre’s vision and contribution to the Greater Vernon community.

Key Responsibilities of the Executive Director:

1.     Strategic and Organizational Leadership

Provide operational leadership to GVMA, implementing the strategic plan and developing operational plans for staff.
Oversee museum operations, programming, collections, archives, facilities, and visitor experience.
Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and forward-thinking organizational culture.
Providing recommendations to the board to identify opportunities to strengthen GVMA’s visibility, relevance, and contribution to the community.

2.     GVCC Planning and Transition

Lead the GVMA’s engagement with community partners throughout the planning and transition to the GVCC.
Identify GVMA’s operational, staffing, financial, facility, and service needs within the new shared space.
Collaborate with GVCC partners to develop a sustainable operating model, including roles, responsibilities, governance, shared resources, communication, and decision-making processes.
Support transition planning, operational readiness, and the development of agreements and protocols required for operating multiple sites.

3.     Community Engagement

Represent GVMA positively and professionally to government, community organizations, Indigenous communities, educational institutions, funders, donors, and cultural partners.
Develop and maintain strong, respectful, and mutually beneficial community relationships.
Engage diverse stakeholders to understand needs, gather feedback, identify opportunities, and support informed decision-making.
Participate in relevant committees, working groups, and initiatives related to GVMA and GVCC.

4.     Financial Management, Fundraising and Revenue Development

Develop and oversee annual operating budgets, financial plans, and expenditure controls, while working in collaboration with the Treasurer and Finance Committee.
Oversee grant applications, fundraising, donor development, sponsorships, and revenue-generating initiatives.
Support financial planning for the GVCC transition, including shared costs, funding requirements, and revenue opportunities.
Ensure sound financial stewardship and compliance with applicable requirements.

5.     People, Culture and Organizational Development

Lead, support, and develop staff, contractors, and volunteers.
Oversee recruitment, performance management, training and development, and succession planning.
Maintain human resources policies and the employee handbook to ensure equitable and fair treatment of all employees, while working in collaboration with the HR Committee.
Promote a respectful, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.

6.     Operations, Programming and Visitor Experience

Oversee the effective day-to-day operation of GVMA and the delivery of high-quality services and programs.
Support exhibitions, educational activities, events, research, and community programming.
Ensure the responsible stewardship, preservation, and interpretation of collections and archival resources.
Promote an engaging, welcoming, accessible, and inclusive visitor experience that match the needs of Greater Vernon.

7.     Governance and Accountability

Report regularly to the Board of Directors on operations, financial performance, strategic priorities and risks, while also collaborating frequently with the Board President.
Prepare reports, recommendations, and supporting materials for Board meetings and the Annual General Meeting.
Maintain effective communication with the RDNO and other relevant governing and funding bodies.
Implement Board-approved policies, strategic directions, and initiatives.
Ensure compliance with the Society’s Constitution, Bylaws, policies, and applicable legislation.

Required Qualifications and Experience:

The ideal candidate will be an experienced and collaborative leader who can balance organizational stewardship with the relationship-building, planning, and change leadership required to support GVMA's future. The following are the desired education, skills and experience:

A bachelor’s degree in museum studies, history, business administration, public administration, non-profit management, arts administration, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and relevant leadership experience may be considered.
A minimum of five years of progressive management or leadership experience in a museum, cultural institution, nonprofit organization, public-sector organization, or related environment.
Demonstrated experience providing strategic and operational leadership in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
Experience developing and managing operating budgets, financial plans, funding proposals, and grant applications.
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining effective relationships with community organizations, government representatives, funders, donors, and other stakeholders.
Strong communication, negotiation, facilitation, and relationship-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to engage diverse groups, understand competing needs, build consensus, and move collaborative initiatives forward.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, develop, and retain staff and volunteers.
Experience leading or supporting organizational change, strategic planning, facility development, organizational growth, or a significant transition is an asset.
A commitment to ethical leadership, accountability, inclusion, accessibility, and respect for diverse cultures, abilities, and backgrounds.

new_jobs.description:
We Are Banking At Another Level.

Choosing BDC as your employer
means working in a healthy, inclusive, and skilled workplace that puts forward the best conditions to bring together unique teams where employees are empowered to act. It also means being at the centre of ambitious economic and financial projects to see further and to do things differently, to fuel the success of Canadian entrepreneurs.

Flexible and competitive benefits, including an Employee Savings and Investment Plan where BDC matches part of your voluntary contributions, a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, a $750 wellness and health care spending account, to name a few
In addition to paid vacation each year, five personal days, sick days as necessary, and our offices are closed from December 25 to January 1
A hybrid work model that truly balances work and personal life
Opportunities for learning, training and development, and much more...

Explore the BDC Way in our Culture Book

Join a team shaping Canada’s venture capital ecosystem

At BDC, the Government Funds team manages capital on behalf of the Government of Canada to strengthen and grow Canada’s venture capital market. This includes deploying $350M under the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP)
, $450M under the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (VCCI)
, and $450M under the Renewed Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Renewed VCCI)
. These programs totalling $1.2B AUM are designed to crowd in private capital
and support fund managers across the Canadian venture capital asset class.

Building on this foundation, BDC is now deploying the $1B Growth Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Growth VCCI)
, a landmark platform focused on scaling Canada’s most promising funds and innovative companies.

This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of investment, policy, and ecosystem development
, with direct exposure to the most prominent Canadian fund managers while contributing to a national priority initiative shaping Canada’s innovation economy
.

Position Overview

As Director, you will combine leadership, investment expertise, and complex project management to support the deployment and oversight of government-backed venture capital programs, including VCAP, VCCI, Renewed VCCI, and upcoming Growth VCCI.

You will play a lead role in investment execution, stakeholder management, and portfolio governance, while engaging closely with fund managers, institutional partners, and internal stakeholders including Government.

CHALLENGES TO BE MET

Investment Expertise

Lead complex business and legal negotiations with fund managers and external stakeholders for execution of program delivery including fund investments.
Provide strategic oversight of investment activities across the portfolio, ensuring alignment between policy objectives, portfolio construction considerations, and market dynamics
Provide senior investment judgment and guidance on fund performance, risk management, and portfolio development matters

Fund Oversight & Governance

Serve as BDC’s representative on portfolio funds’ LPACs and other governance bodies
Monitor fund performance, governance, and compliance with fund agreements and program requirements
Provide strategic insight and constructive challenge to support strong governance practices and enhance fund outcomes
Guide fund managers on governance and operational best practices to strengthen the long-term sustainability of the venture capital ecosystem

Leadership and Team Management

Demonstrate leadership in team meetings and operations processes, ensuring effective resource allocation, quality control, operational excellence, and alignment with strategic priorities
Ensure the timely and accurate execution of operational activities, including capital calls, distributions, reporting, and stakeholder deliverables
Provide coaching, mentorship, and leadership to a team of Analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture focused on continuous improvement and professional development
Identify capability and capacity gaps, oversee recruitment and onboarding activities, and promote knowledge sharing and best practices across the team

Program Delivery & Stakeholder Management

Provide strategic input into the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of current and future government investment programs
Respond to complex and time-sensitive requests from internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a high standard of service and professionalism
Oversee the preparation and dissemination of quarterly and annual reporting, performance dashboards, and stakeholder communications
Ensure high standards of quality, consistency, accuracy, and timeliness across all reporting outputs and program deliverables

Portfolio & Ecosystem Leadership

Build and maintain strong relationships with fund managers, institutional investors, ecosystem stakeholders, and government partners
Represent BDC Capital and Government Funds at industry conferences, panels, events, and stakeholder forums
Stay closely connected to venture capital trends, market developments, and emerging opportunities to support strategic decision-making
Support and lead thought leadership initiatives, market studies, and research projects that generate insights from government investment programs and portfolio activities

What We Are Looking For

Experience and qualifications

Minimum of a Bachelor degree in Commerce or a related discipline (finance, accounting, law or business administration preferred), or an equivalent combination of academic training and relevant professional experience
10 years+ experience in venture capital, private equity, or growth investing, with direct exposure to deal-making at the fund level as well as investment underwriting, structuring, business and legal negotiations and execution
Demonstrated expertise in venture capital fund structures, LPAs, governance frameworks, and policy-driven investment programs
Demonstrated ability to lead complex negotiations and manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously
Significant experience serving on LPACs, Boards of Directors, or equivalent governance bodies
Ability to manage complex stakeholder relationships involving fund managers, institutional investors, government representatives, and senior executives
Strong understanding of the Canadian venture capital ecosystem and a well-established network of industry relationships
Experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams

Core competencies

Strong strategic and investment judgment
Demonstrated leadership and people management capabilities
Excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills
Ability to align operational execution with broader policy, program, and organizational objectives
High level of rigour, organization, and attention to detail
Ability to operate effectively in a complex, fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environment
Collaborative mindset with a commitment to team development, knowledge sharing, and excellence

The position is primarily based in Montreal or Ottawa, with a preference for these locations. Toronto is also acceptable.

We are dedicated to providing an environment where all employees feel valued, respected and able to reach their full potential. Proudly one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers
and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers

If you require an accommodation to complete your application, please do not hesitate to contact us at accessibility@bdc.ca.

While we appreciate all applications, we advise that only the candidates selected to participate in the recruitment process will be contacted.
